open_points.subject: K-02 purity vs A03 sandbox filesystem access
open_points.text: K-02 says a function has "no filesystem beyond its input"; A03 rule 1 gives "one private exchange directory" and rule 4 only traps "opening any path outside the exchange directory and the read-only runtime".
open_points.question: Should function code be allowed to read/write files inside the sandbox exchange directory, or should any filesystem access by user code be a violation?
options: Allow filesystem access inside the exchange directory (and runtime read-only paths)
Forbid all filesystem access from function code, including exchange directory paths
open_points.default_guess: Allow exchange-directory access, because A03 explicitly permits it and only blocks paths outside it.

open_points.subject: A11 recovery timestamp mapping
open_points.text: A11 rule 4: "writes it with status outcome_unknown, its start time taken from the EffectAttempt and its end time the time of recovery".
open_points.question: Which exact EffectAttempt field populates NodeExecution.started_at during in-flight recovery?
options: Use recovery time for both started_at and ended_at

open_points.subject: A14/A15 ordering by (node_id, map_index)
open_points.text: A14 rule 2 orders resend "in (`node_id`, `map_index`) order — an element without `map_index` before index 0"; A15 rule 1 reuses this order for trace writes.
open_points.question: How is `map_index` compared (numeric ascending, string/code-point, or another rule)?
options: Numeric ascending integers after the no-map_index case
String/code-point comparison of rendered index values

open_points.subject: A09 path placeholder integer rendering
open_points.text: A09 rule 2: each `{name}` in the path must be a non-null string or integer and is percent-encoded.
open_points.question: What exact textual form is used for integer placeholder values before percent-encoding?
options: Reject integer placeholders and require strings at send time
open_points.default_guess: Canonical JSON integer form (decimal, no extra formatting).

open_points.subject: A08 manifest record shape checks
open_points.text: A08 rule 5 defines manifest mismatch checks (missing fields, duplicate capability names, absent operation, etc.) but does not fully define handling of wrong JSON types/structures for those fields.
open_points.question: When manifest fields exist but have wrong types (for example `capabilities` not an array, entries not objects, header maps not object-of-strings), which exact check fails first and with what classification?
options: Treat any type/shape mismatch as manifest mismatch at the earliest field-specific check
Treat malformed structures as if fields/entries are absent
open_points.default_guess: Fail as manifest mismatch at the earliest field-specific check, with no coercion.
